title: Osteoclast Visualization Using NewFuchsin TRAP Staining for Bone Tissue
author: Nakamura, Kawaai, et al.

steps.title: Prepare TRAP staining solution
steps.instruction: In a micro‑test tube mix 10 µL NewFuchsin stock solution with 10 µL sodium nitrite stock solution, incubate at room temperature for 1 min; add 1 mL TRAP buffer, then add 10 µL naphthol AS‑BI phosphate stock solution and mix to obtain ~1.0 mL working solution sufficient for one slide.

steps.title: Apply staining to bone sections
steps.instruction: Gently drop the working solution onto each decalcified paraffin bone section on a glass slide, place the slide in a moisture chamber to prevent drying, and incubate at room temperature for 10–20 min (or at 37 °C if coloration is weak).

steps.title: Rinse stained sections
steps.instruction: Rinse the slides thoroughly with tap water to remove excess stain.

steps.title: Coverslip with non‑aqueous medium
steps.instruction: Mount the rinsed sections with a coverslip using a non‑aqueous mounting medium.

steps.title: Observe stained sections
steps.instruction: Examine the slides by bright‑field microscopy and by fluorescence microscopy; when detecting fluorescence, use an excitation filter appropriate for rhodamine.

steps.title: Whole‑mount staining and clearing
steps.instruction: Stain whole bone pieces with NewFuchsin TRAP as above, then place the stained bone in a 1.5‑mL polypropylene tube and clear the tissue by immersion in ethyl cinnamate.

steps.title: Observe cleared whole bone
steps.instruction: Image the ethyl cinnamate‑cleared bone using a confocal laser‑scanning microscope equipped with a fluorescence detector.
